# Whitepaper Reading Guide {.unnumbered}

The [section index](index.qmd) lists all 27 papers as a flat table —
good for lookup, silent on how the papers relate to each other or what
order to read them in. This page groups them into tracks and proposes
reading paths for common audiences. It is a companion to the index, not
a replacement, and states no doctrine of its own — every claim below is
about the papers' own content and status, not a canon claim.

## The corpus at a glance

The section splits into two genres:

- **Policy/architecture papers** — Executive Summary → numbered
  sections → Honest Limits → Conclusion. These state UIAO's governance
  doctrine and map it onto a compliance framework (ZTMM, BOD-25-01,
  FedRAMP).
- **Narrative papers** — an "In this whitepaper" overview → Act/Part
  structure → a canon-mapping table → Provenance. These tell an
  operational or historical story and derive the doctrine from it
  rather than stating it up front.

Three papers — [`ad-to-entraid-migration-problem`](ad-to-entraid-migration-problem.qmd),
[`aodim-executive-whitepaper`](aodim-executive-whitepaper.qmd), and
[`uiao-vs-native-tools`](uiao-vs-native-tools.qmd) — predate both
genres: they're docx imports from before the canon-anchoring convention
existed. They carry real content (the original business case for the
whole program) but are the corpus's least structurally current papers;
read them for the argument, not as a canon-anchored reference.

## Start here if your question is "who does this mandate bind"

[Federal Compliance for Moderate Agencies](federal-compliance-for-moderate-agencies.qmd)
sits outside the six tracks below by design — it's a short primer, not a
deep-dive, and its job is disambiguation and routing rather than argument.
If the question in front of you is "does FedRAMP 20x apply to my agency or
to our cloud provider," or "what's actually a hard deadline versus
guidance," read it first; it routes into whichever track below actually
answers your follow-up question. Everyone else should skip straight to the
tracks.

## Six tracks

Papers are grouped by the question they answer, not by filename.
Several papers earn a place in more than one track — that's
cross-listed, not a mistake.

### Track 1 — Governance Foundations

Start here for "what is UIAO."

| Paper | Status | Role |
|---|---|---|
| [UIAO Governance OS](uiao-governance-os-whitepaper.qmd) | Active | **Flagship.** Defines the substrate, the three operating principles, the evidence chain. Everything downstream assumes this. |
| [Zero Trust Governance](zero-trust-governance-whitepaper.qmd) | Active | Maps the substrate onto CISA's five ZTMM pillars, pillar by pillar. |
| [Zero Trust Governance Principles](zero-trust-governance-principles.qmd) | Active | Broader and newer than the paper above — whole-agency (Network+CSP+VMware) scope, cross-cutting capabilities, the "why programs stall below Advanced" argument. Read immediately after it, not standalone. |
| [Modernization Governance](modernization-governance-whitepaper.qmd) | Active | Governance framing specifically for the AD → Entra ID migration — the bridge into Track 2. |

::: {.callout-note}
## Two papers, one arc — pick the one your audience needs

*Federal Application Aware Networking Architecture* and *From Mainframe
to Application-Aware Modernization* are siblings, not a sequence: the
former is the external, vendor-neutral pitch (hand it to an audience
wary of a platform commitment); the latter is the internal,
canon-anchored version (hand it to a team that has already adopted
UIAO and needs the ADR trail). Handing the wrong one to an audience is
the single most common mis-sequencing risk in this corpus.
:::

## Recommended reading paths

Pick the path that matches why the reader opened the site, not the
alphabetical file list.

**A federal CIO/CISO with 30 minutes (first exposure)**

1. [UIAO Governance OS](uiao-governance-os-whitepaper.qmd) — what the substrate is and why "operating system," not "framework."
2. [Federal Application Aware Networking Architecture](federal-application-aware-networking-architecture.qmd) — the compliance-deadline argument (FedRAMP 20x) and its Call to Action, written to be handed off without modification.

**An assessor validating BOD-25-01 / ZTMM claims**

0. [Federal Compliance for Moderate Agencies](federal-compliance-for-moderate-agencies.qmd) — confirm which mandates in play actually bind the agency you're assessing versus its vendors, before diving into any one of them.
1. [Assessment Tools vs. Closing BOD-25-01 Findings](bod-25-01-close-before-assess.qmd) — the sequencing argument.
2. [SCuBAGear Integration](scubagear-integration-whitepaper.qmd) → [ZTA and SCuBA — How They Relate](zta-scuba-relationship.qmd) — how the evidence is produced and how it differs from Microsoft's own assessment.
3. [Zero Trust Governance Principles](zero-trust-governance-principles.qmd) — the maturity-model context for what "closed" is being measured against.
4. [Ticket-to-Machine, Not Ticket-to-Human](ticket-to-machine-not-ticket-to-human.qmd) — how closure evidence is distinguished from a changed setting.

**A network/infrastructure architect**

1. [Federal Application Aware Networking Architecture](federal-application-aware-networking-architecture.qmd) — the full arc and the physics argument.
2. [SD-WAN vs. DIA Under TIC 3.0](tic3-sdwan-vs-dia.qmd) and [Next Generation DNS](infoblox-hybrid-dns-unified-ddi.qmd) — read in either order; both sit under Act 4 independently.
3. [UIAO Git Server Interfaces](git-server-interfaces-whitepaper.qmd) — once a UIAO deployment is actually being planned.

**An identity/directory team running an AD → Entra ID modernization**

1. [AD-to-Entra ID Structural Migration Problem](ad-to-entraid-migration-problem.qmd) — the original problem statement.
2. [Modernization Governance](modernization-governance-whitepaper.qmd) → [From Mainframe to Application-Aware Modernization](modernization-journey.qmd) — governance framing, then the canon-anchored arc.
3. [Flipping 50,000 Devices to Hybrid Join](hybrid-join-without-governance.qmd) — the first concrete operation to execute inside that arc.
4. [Federal SSOT Alignment](federal-ssot-alignment.qmd) — the data-governance-mandate framing of the same event.

**Someone evaluating UIAO against Microsoft-native tools or a build-vs-buy decision**

1. [UIAO vs. Native Tools](uiao-vs-native-tools.qmd) — the gap analysis.
2. [OrgPath Composability Matrix](orgpath-composability-matrix.qmd) — what's actually à la carte, so "build vs. buy" isn't a false binary.
3. [Snowflake Key-Pair Conversion — the UIAO and OrgPath Reading](snowflake-keypair-vs-uiao-orgpath.qmd) — a worked example on a platform outside today's boundary, useful for gauging how far the model generalizes.

**Reading the whole corpus, start to finish**

Track 1 (all four) → Track 2 (all six) → Track 3 (all four) → Track 4
(all four) → Track 5 (the two papers not already read in Track 2) →
Track 6 (the two papers not already read in Track 2). This order
front-loads the doctrine (Track 1) before any domain paper assumes it,
and reads the two mainframe-to-Zero-Trust narratives back-to-back
(Track 2 then Track 4) so the vendor-neutral vs. canon-anchored
contrast is visible rather than discovered by accident months apart.
